cli.source.not_found: No source has the key %s. See them all with: michel source list --all
cli.source.read.not_found: No item has the id %q. See them with: michel source items
cli.source.read.usage: Give the id of an item (see michel source items), or --all to mark them all as read.
cli.source.remove.foreign: The folder of %s does not carry Michel's marker for this source: Michel does not delete it. Delete it yourself if it is no longer needed.
cli.source.remove.hidden: %s is hidden. To bring it back: michel source reset %s
cli.source.remove.installed: %s is installed on this computer. Uninstall it before you remove it.
cli.source.remove.needs_yes: Removing %s uninstalls it, and Michel cannot ask the question here. If you agree, run: michel source remove %s --yes
cli.source.remove.will_uninstall: %s is installed in %s: Michel will delete that folder.
cli.source.remove.will_unpin: %s is installed: Michel will forget its version and delete the copy kept in its data folder.
cli.source.reset.done.one: %d source is set back as in Michel's catalog.
cli.source.reset.done.other: %d sources are back as in Michel's catalog.
cli.source.reset.kept: Permissions to contact sites and skills already installed do not change.
cli.source.reset.purge_needs_yes: Deleting your sources needs your confirmation, but Michel cannot ask the question here. Read the list above. If you agree, run: michel source reset --all --purge-user --yes
cli.source.reset.purge_refused: Nothing changed: your sources are kept.
cli.source.reset.user: %s is a source you added: "reset" only works for the sources of Michel's catalog. To remove it: michel source remove %s
cli.source.run.audit_failed: %s on %s: the findings are saved, but Michel could not write the audit log: %v. Check that the data folder is writable.
cli.source.run.need_project: Name the project to check: michel source run %s --project <name>
cli.source.run.no_rules: Semgrep has no rules to run: Michel runs it offline, with only the rules (YAML files) of the folder plugins/semgrep/rules in its data folder. Put your rules there, then run it again.
cli.source.run.not_installed: %s is not installed on this machine (Michel looks for the program %s on the PATH). Install it, or give its report: michel source run %s --project %s --input <report>
cli.source.run.not_plugin: %s is not a plugin: only a plugin can be run (michel source list --kind plugin).
cli.source.run.not_runnable: Michel does not run %s itself. Produce its report yourself (SARIF), then give it: michel source run %s --project %s --input <report>
cli.source.run.off: %s is off. Enable it first: michel source enable %s
cli.source.run.report_too_big: The report of %s is too big for Michel (more than %d results or %d MB): nothing was changed. Narrow the analysis (fewer folders or rules), then run it again.
cli.source.run.skipped_known.one: ; %d flaw already found by the OSV scan is left out
cli.source.run.skipped_known.other: ; %d flaws already found by the OSV scan are left out

cli.source.show.host_missing: Michel contacts %s (for: %s). There is no rule yet: when you turn the source on, Michel asks for your consent.
cli.source.show.status: Repository state on %s: %d stars, last change on %s, latest commit %s
cli.source.show.status_new_version: New version available: %s (pinned: %s). To see the changes: michel source upgrade %s
cli.source.show.status_none: Repository state: not read yet (michel source update reads it).

cli.source.update.rate_limited.other: · %[2]s: the source asked Michel to slow down after %[1]d items; what was read is kept and the next update goes on
cli.source.update.some_failed.one: %d source could not be read; Michel keeps its previous data.
cli.source.update.some_failed.other: %d sources could not be read; Michel keeps their previous data.

cli.source.upgrade.done_mcp: %s is pinned at version %s. If the server runs from this code, restart it.
cli.source.upgrade.folder_changes: The skill changes its name in this version: its folder moves from %s to %s. If you agree, Michel installs it in the new folder and deletes the old one.
cli.source.upgrade.needs_yes: Upgrading %s needs your consent, but Michel cannot ask the question here. Read the text above. If you agree, run: michel source upgrade %s --yes
cli.source.upgrade.not_installed: %s is not installed. To install it: michel source install %s
cli.source.upgrade.nothing: No new version of %s is known. michel source update checks the repository every day.
cli.source.upgrade.skill_md: Lines of SKILL.md removed (-) and added (+):

cli.tech.none: You declared no technology besides those of your projects. To add one: michel tech add nginx

digest.exploited_decided.other: %d exploited flaws you deferred or ignored

explain.label.kev_yes: yes, exploited in the wild (CISA KEV list)

fix.cause.agent_ended: the agent ended without a proposal
fix.cause.agent_start_failed: Claude Code could not be started: %s
fix.cause.apply_failed: Michel could not create the fix branch: %s.
fix.cause.exit: Claude Code ended with an error
fix.cause.gone_not_merged: the flaw no longer shows in the scan, but the branch is not merged: Michel cannot tell what fixed it
fix.cause.mask_token: the change holds a placeholder standing for a secret
fix.cause.merged_still_seen: the branch is merged, but the flaw still shows in the scan
fix.cause.prepare_failed: Michel could not prepare the copy: %s
fix.cause.restarted: Michel was restarted while the agent worked
fix.cause.timeout: the attempt reached its time limit
fix.consent.external_providers: By accepting, you allow external AI providers in your policy (setting ai.external_providers_enabled).
fix.consent.install: Michel downloads the packages the copy needs from %s.
fix.consent.runs_code: Michel runs composer/npm and your tests on a copy, with your Windows rights; the code written by the agent runs.
fix.consent.sensitive: This project is classified sensitive: secrets are masked and the excluded files are not copied.
fix.consent.what_leaves: What leaves your computer: the code of the copy the agent reads, the brief (secrets masked) and your messages. Not the excluded files, not the secrets.
fix.err.agent_gone: The agent's session has ended: your message cannot reach it. Start a new fix.
fix.err.agent_unavailable: Michel cannot use Claude Code right now. Check that it is installed and logged in, then try again.
fix.err.bad_state: This fix cannot do that at this stage. Reload the page to see where it stands.
fix.err.busy: A fix is already in progress on this project. Finish it or refuse it first.
fix.err.change_refused: Michel refused the agent's change: it touched files outside the copy, or a file Michel protects. Nothing was applied.
fix.err.consent_required: Before an agent works on this project, Michel needs your agreement for what leaves your computer.
fix.err.health_forbidden: This project is classified health: Michel never sends its code to an external AI. You can read the brief and fix it by hand.
fix.err.mask_token: The change holds a placeholder standing for a secret ([secret-…]). Michel hides your secrets before showing them to the agent and never puts one in a branch.
fix.err.no_change: The copy holds no change: there is nothing to propose.
fix.err.no_proposal: This attempt has no proposal yet. Wait for the agent to finish.
fix.err.not_found: Michel does not know this finding or this fix attempt. Reload the page.
fix.err.not_git: This project is not tracked by git: Michel cannot prepare a fix. You can still read the brief.
fix.err.stale_proposal: The proposal changed since you read it. Michel applied nothing; read the new one.
fix.err.strict_local: Your policy is strict_local: external AI providers stay off. To let Michel use Claude Code, switch the policy to standard mode first.
fix.msg.applied: The branch %s is ready. Merge it, then deploy with PhpStorm as usual.
fix.msg.install_refused: Michel did not install the dependencies: %s. The tests were not run.
fix.msg.install_unsupported: Michel can only install dependencies with composer and npm: nothing was installed and the tests were not run.
fix.msg.mask_token: The change holds a placeholder standing for a secret ([secret-…]). Michel never puts one in a branch. Remove it and propose again.
fix.msg.no_change: The copy holds no change: nothing to propose.
fix.msg.proposed: Proposal recorded. It waits for your decision on the page.
fix.msg.rescan_clean: Re-scan of the copy: %s is gone.
fix.msg.rescan_dirty: Re-scan of the copy: %s is still there.
fix.msg.rescan_failed: Re-scan of the copy: Michel could not scan it (%s).
fix.msg.secret_hits.one: %d secret seems written in your code (%s): the agent can read it. To keep it out, exclude the file in the project's settings.
fix.msg.secret_hits.other: %d secrets seem written in your code (%s): the agent can read them. To keep them out, exclude the files in the project's settings.
fix.msg.tests_none: Tests: not run, no test command is configured for this project.
fix.msg.update_refused: Michel did not run the update: %s. The fix starts from the project's current files.
glossary.breaking: a change that can make code written for the old version stop working
glossary.cve: a public identifier for a known security flaw
glossary.cvss: a 0 to 10 score of how severe a flaw is
glossary.kev: a list of flaws that attackers are known to exploit in the wild
glossary.lockfile: the file that records the exact versions installed
glossary.transitive: a package your project does not ask for itself, but that another package needs
notify.fix_waiting.body.one: %d fix waits for your decision. Open the page to read it.
notify.fix_waiting.body.other: %d fixes wait for your decision. Open the page to read them.
notify.fix_waiting.title: %s · a fix waits for you
notify.test.body: This is a test message from Michel: if you can read it, this channel works. It holds no data about your projects.
notify.test.subject: %s · test message
source.consent.discover: Michel will ask %s which public projects are the most followed on a few topics. Only the names of these topics leave, plus your GitHub token if you gave one (GitHub then knows it is you).
source.consent.enrichment: Michel will contact %s to download a public list about vulnerabilities. Nothing from your projects leaves: it is a download.
source.consent.enrichment_on_demand: Michel will send the CVE numbers of your findings (the official code of each vulnerability) to %s. Nothing else leaves.
source.consent.feed: Michel will contact %s to read a security feed. Nothing from your projects leaves: it is a download.
source.consent.osv: Michel will contact %s to download a public vulnerability database. Nothing from your projects leaves: it is a download.
source.consent.repo: Michel will contact %s to read a public project: what it contains and the chosen version. If you gave a GitHub token, GitHub will know it is you.
source.note.discover.github: Lists the most followed GitHub projects on the mcp-security and claude-skills topics. You choose the ones you add.
source.note.enrich.circl: European vulnerability database, another source than the NVD (the official US database). Michel sends the CVE numbers of your findings.
source.note.enrich.epss: Estimates the chance that attackers use a vulnerability within 30 days. Michel downloads the file of the day: nothing is sent.
source.note.enrich.kev: Official list of the vulnerabilities attackers already use. Michel downloads the whole list: nothing about you is sent.
source.note.enrich.nvd: Fills in missing severity scores (CVSS). This service is slow and limits the number of requests. A key (michel secret set nvd-api-key) raises that limit. Michel sends CVE numbers.
source.note.enrich.vulnrichment: Adds a severity score (CVSS) and other ratings (SSVC, CWE) to the vulnerabilities that have none. Michel sends the CVE numbers of your findings.
source.note.feed.angular: Security advisories of Angular. The vulnerabilities of the library itself are already in the OSV database.
source.note.feed.apache_httpd: Vulnerabilities of the Apache 2.4 web server. Michel does not know the versions on your servers yet.
source.note.feed.apple: Security updates of Apple systems and apps.
source.note.feed.atlassian: Security advisories of Atlassian products (Jira, Confluence...).
source.note.feed.cocoapods: Security advisories of the CocoaPods repository.
source.note.feed.containerd: Security advisories of containerd, which runs the containers.
source.note.feed.debian: Debian security advisories. These vulnerabilities already come through the OSV Debian database.
source.note.feed.drupal: Drupal security advisories. The drupal/* modules are already partly followed through OSV.
source.note.feed.envoy: Security advisories of Envoy (a relay between servers).
source.note.feed.jenkins: Security advisories of Jenkins and its plugins.
source.note.feed.laravel: Security advisories of Laravel. The vulnerabilities of the library itself are already in the OSV database.
source.note.feed.nextjs: Security advisories of Next.js. The vulnerabilities of the library itself are already in the OSV database.
source.note.feed.nginx: Security advisories of the nginx web server. Michel does not know the versions on your servers yet.
source.note.feed.nodejs: Security releases of Node.js itself. Michel does not know your Node.js version yet.
source.note.feed.openssh: Vulnerabilities of OpenSSH. Michel does not know the versions on your servers yet.
source.note.feed.openssl: Vulnerabilities of OpenSSL. Michel does not know the versions on your servers yet.
source.note.feed.php: Security news of PHP itself. Michel does not know your PHP version yet.
source.note.feed.postgresql: Vulnerabilities of the PostgreSQL database. Michel does not know the versions on your servers yet.
source.note.feed.rails: Security announcements of Ruby on Rails.
source.note.feed.react: Security advisories of React. The vulnerabilities of the library itself are already in the OSV database.
source.note.feed.runc: Security advisories of runc, which starts the containers.
source.note.feed.symfony: Symfony security posts. The vulnerabilities of the library itself are already in the OSV database.
source.note.feed.vue: Security advisories of Vue.js. The vulnerabilities of the library itself are already in the OSV database.
source.note.mcp.cve_search: Queries a CVE-Search server. Prefer a server you host yourself: the CVE numbers you look for are sent to it.
source.note.mcp.safedep_vet: Checks npm and PyPI packages for known vulnerabilities and malware.
source.note.mcp.semgrep: Lets your coding AI read your code again to look for vulnerabilities. This server now ships inside the semgrep program.
source.note.mcp.wazuh: Reads the security alerts of a Wazuh monitoring tool. Useful once Michel can read the logs of your servers.
source.note.osv.almalinux: Software installed on a AlmaLinux server. Useful once Michel can list what is installed on your servers.
source.note.osv.alpine: Software installed on a Alpine server. Useful once Michel can list what is installed on your servers.
source.note.osv.android: Android platform and components. Michel does not scan these projects yet.
source.note.osv.chainguard: Software installed on a Chainguard server. Useful once Michel can list what is installed on your servers.
source.note.osv.crates_io: Rust packages. Michel does not scan these projects yet.
source.note.osv.debian: Software installed on a Debian server. Useful once Michel can list what is installed on your servers.
source.note.osv.github_actions: Automatic steps (GitHub Actions) used in the GitHub automations of your project. Michel does not read them yet.
source.note.osv.go: Go modules. Michel does not scan these projects yet.
source.note.osv.hex: Erlang and Elixir packages. Michel does not scan these projects yet.
source.note.osv.malicious: Packages booby-trapped by attackers (marked MAL-). They are already in the other OSV databases: no need to add it.
source.note.osv.maven: Java packages (Maven). Michel does not scan these projects yet.
source.note.osv.npm: JavaScript packages. Needed to scan the projects that have a package-lock.json, yarn.lock or pnpm-lock.yaml file.
source.note.osv.nuget: .NET packages. Michel does not scan these projects yet.
source.note.osv.opensuse: Software installed on a openSUSE server. Useful once Michel can list what is installed on your servers.
source.note.osv.packagist: PHP packages. Needed to scan the projects that have a composer.lock file.
source.note.osv.pub: Dart and Flutter packages. Michel does not scan these projects yet.
source.note.osv.pypi: Python packages. Michel does not scan these projects yet.
source.note.osv.red_hat: Software installed on a Red Hat server. Useful once Michel can list what is installed on your servers.
source.note.osv.rocky_linux: Software installed on a Rocky Linux server. Useful once Michel can list what is installed on your servers.
source.note.osv.rubygems: Ruby packages. Michel does not scan these projects yet.
source.note.osv.suse: Software installed on a SUSE server. Useful once Michel can list what is installed on your servers.
source.note.osv.swifturl: Swift packages. Michel does not scan these projects yet.
source.note.osv.ubuntu: Software installed on a Ubuntu server. Useful once Michel can list what is installed on your servers.
source.note.osv.wolfi: Software installed on a Wolfi server. Useful once Michel can list what is installed on your servers.
source.note.plugin.codeql: Reads a report of CodeQL (a code analysis tool) made elsewhere, for example by your continuous integration. CodeQL does not handle PHP. Check its licence terms too.
source.note.plugin.semgrep: Static analysis of your PHP and JavaScript code, with rules you write yourself.
source.note.plugin.trivy: Spots setting mistakes in your Docker, compose or Kubernetes files. Michel runs it without an internet connection, on your projects.
source.note.plugin.zap: Reads a report of ZAP, a tool that attacks a site to test it. Run it on a test copy, never on your real site.
source.note.ref.awesome_agent_skills: A list of skills for coding AIs, to browse.
source.note.ref.awesome_claude_skills: A list of Claude skills, to browse.
source.note.ref.awesome_cybersecurity_ag: A list of security AI agents, to browse.
source.note.ref.awesome_mcp_security: Tools to check the security of MCP servers themselves (MCP-scan, MCP-Shield).
source.note.ref.cve_org: The official register of CVE numbers. The OSV database already contains them.
source.note.ref.dependency_track: A tool to send the list of the components of your software to (SBOM). It is not a source of vulnerabilities.
source.note.ref.deps_dev: Information about packages. Michel does not need it: it already knows how to compare versions.
source.note.ref.first_cvss: The organisation that created the CVSS severity scores.
source.note.ref.haproxy: Project site. It offers no security advisory feed.
source.note.ref.openldap: Project site. It offers no security advisory feed.
source.note.ref.openssf_scorecard: Health score of open source projects. Michel could use it later.
source.note.ref.trailofbits_skills: Skills by Trail of Bits, to browse.
source.note.ref.wireguard: Project site. It offers no security advisory feed.
source.note.skill.claude_code_owasp: Recognised security guidelines (OWASP Top 10 2025, ASVS 5.0) for the AI that fixes your code. Few people follow this project: read its content before you install it.
source.note.skill.trailofbits_code_audit: A skill to find the other places where a vulnerability you already found occurs (with CodeQL or Semgrep queries), made by a recognised security firm.
source.trust.archived: Archived by its author: it is no longer maintained. Check it before relying on it.
source.trust.unchecked: Repository state not read yet (michel source update reads it).
source.trust.user: Added by you: not in Michel's catalog.
